map.Exempts the business from paying any tax: Lets the business pay a lower tax rate than other firms in town
map.Guarantees that the business will make a: Protects the business from competition from other firms nearby

ww.Lets the business pay a lower tax rate t: A license does not change a firm's tax rate. Businesses pay taxes under tax law whether or not they hold a license, which only grants permission to operate.
ww.Protects the business from competition f: A license does not shield a firm from competitors. Rivals can open nearby, and the license only gives government permission for the business to operate in that location.

map.Free of duty, because the delay was only: Free of duty, because the retailer did not pay in advance
map.Required only to refund the retailer's s: Required to apologize in writing and offer a discount later

ww.Free of duty, because the retailer did n: Paying in advance is not required for a contract to bind the supplier. A signed contract creates a duty to deliver, and failing to do so is a breach.
ww.Required to apologize in writing and off: An apology and a future discount do not repay the retailer's lost sales. The usual remedy for breach is damages covering the losses the failure caused.

map.Avoiding every stressful situation that: Understanding the feelings and needs of your coworkers
map.Hiding your feelings from all of your co: Controlling your impulses so you stay calm under pressure

ww.Understanding the feelings and needs of: Understanding other people's feelings is empathy or social awareness. Self-awareness is about recognizing your own emotions and how they affect what you do.
ww.Controlling your impulses so you stay ca: Controlling impulses and staying calm is self-regulation. Self-awareness comes first and means recognizing your own emotions and their effect on your behavior.

map.It guarantees that no conflicts happen a: It makes employees finish routine tasks at a faster speed
map.It replaces technical skills for any job: It matters mainly for managers and not for entry-level staff

ww.It makes employees finish routine tasks: Emotional intelligence is about understanding and managing emotions, not task speed. Its value shows in communication, teamwork and decision making rather than in faster routine output.
ww.It matters mainly for managers and not f: Emotional intelligence helps staff at every level, from new hires to executives. Anyone who works with coworkers and customers benefits from reading and managing emotions.

map.Hire a large team of staff before the ca: Spend her savings on equipment and decor before testing demand
map.Sign a long lease on a building before r: Copy a competitor's menu and prices without checking her costs

ww.Spend her savings on equipment and decor: Spending savings on equipment before testing demand risks money on an unproven idea. Market research should come first so she learns whether customers will pay her prices.
ww.Copy a competitor's menu and prices with: Copying a competitor ignores her own costs and customers. She needs her own research to learn what her market will pay and whether her prices cover expenses.

map.It replaces the need to serve customers: It lowers the cost of the products a business sells
map.It removes the need for a business plan: It gives the business legal protection from lawsuits
map.It guarantees that the business will suc: It lets a business avoid paying taxes in its first years

ww.It lowers the cost of the products a bus: Networking builds contacts, but it does not change production or purchase costs. Costs fall through suppliers, efficiency and pricing choices, not through meeting people.
ww.It gives the business legal protection f: Legal protection from lawsuits comes from a business structure such as an LLC or corporation. Networking builds relationships and does not change a firm's legal status.
ww.It lets a business avoid paying taxes in: Tax duties do not depend on who an owner knows. Networking can open doors to partners and customers, but taxes are set by law.

map.Having all employees work only on the ni: A schedule that rotates staff between day and night shifts
map.Having employees who are all in one age: Employees who share the same job title and pay level

ww.A schedule that rotates staff between da: A rotating shift schedule is about when people work. Diversity refers to differences among people, such as background, culture, age and experience.
ww.Employees who share the same job title a: Sharing a job title and pay is about job structure. Diversity refers to differences among people in background and perspective, not matching positions.

map.To print employee paychecks and nothing: To track the daily cash held in a store's register
map.To store only the addresses of customers: To advertise products to customers on social media
map.To replace all of the managers in the co: To train new managers in leadership skills

ww.To track the daily cash held in a store': Tracking register cash is a cashiering task. An MIS gathers and organizes information from across the business so managers can plan, control and make decisions.
ww.To advertise products to customers on so: Advertising is a marketing activity. An MIS is a system that organizes business information into reports that help managers decide.
ww.To train new managers in leadership skil: Training is a human resources function. An MIS supplies information, such as reports and summaries, that managers use when planning and deciding.

map.Ship the goods to customers only once ea: Produce goods in large batches to lower the cost per unit
map.Hold very large safety stocks at all tim: Keep a full warehouse so orders can be filled from stock

ww.Produce goods in large batches to lower: Large batch production builds up inventory, which is the opposite of JIT. JIT brings in small amounts just when they are needed to cut storage costs.
ww.Keep a full warehouse so orders can be f: A full warehouse ties up money and space in stored goods. JIT tries to keep inventory low by receiving items close to when they are needed.

map.Using the same script with every custome: Giving customers a coupon for the most popular product
map.Giving every single customer identical o: Speeding up calls to handle as many customers as possible
map.Refusing to remember any of the returnin: Training staff to follow a strict return policy

ww.Giving customers a coupon for the most p: A coupon for a popular item is the same for everyone. Personalizing means matching service to what each customer needs and prefers.
ww.Speeding up calls to handle as many cust: Faster calls focus on speed and volume. Personalizing takes time to learn what an individual customer wants and to adjust the service to fit.
ww.Training staff to follow a strict return: A return policy is a rule that applies to everyone alike. Personalizing service uses what you know about a customer to tailor the experience.

map.A market with two equal sellers of the s: A market with a few large sellers who watch each other's prices
map.A market where only the buyers set the p: A market with many sellers each offering a slightly different product

ww.A market with a few large sellers who wa: A few large sellers describe an oligopoly. A monopoly has just one seller, so the firm faces no direct rivals offering a close substitute.
ww.A market with many sellers each offering: Many sellers offering differentiated products describe monopolistic competition. A monopoly has a single seller with no close substitutes.

map.Nothing at all, so the page is left blan: The pay they hope to earn in the new job
map.A list of every game that you have ever: Their social media handles and favorite hobbies

ww.The pay they hope to earn in the new job: Pay expectations usually do not belong on a resume. A resume should show skills, activities and experience that prove the applicant can do the job.
ww.Their social media handles and favorite: Social media handles and hobbies do not show job skills. A resume should highlight school activities, volunteering and skills that relate to the work.

map.To set the tax rate on every sale of goo: To set the prices businesses can charge for goods in a state
map.To replace the need for written contract: To protect new business names from copying by other firms

ww.To set the prices businesses can charge: The UCC does not control prices. It sets common rules for sales contracts so that trade between states works smoothly, while prices are set by the market.
ww.To protect new business names from copyi: Protecting business names is the job of trademark and name registration laws. The UCC deals with commercial transactions such as sales of goods.

map.Declining to sign a contract of sale at: Breaking a promise made in a signed contract
map.Following every safety rule perfectly at: Copying another firm's logo for your own products

ww.Breaking a promise made in a signed cont: Breaking a signed contract is breach of contract. Negligence is a failure to use reasonable care that causes harm, even when no promise was broken.
ww.Copying another firm's logo for your own: Copying a logo is trademark infringement. Negligence is a failure to use reasonable care that results in harm to another person.

map.Employers must provide a reason for ever: Employers must prove cause before they can end the job
map.Employees can be fired only after a writ: Employees hold the job for a fixed term set by contract

ww.Employers must prove cause before they c: Proving cause is needed under a contract with job protection, not under at-will employment. At-will employers may end the job for any lawful reason without proof.
ww.Employees hold the job for a fixed term: A fixed term set by contract is not at-will. At-will jobs have no set end date, so either side can end the relationship at any time.

map.Hiring only workers with disabilities an: Equal pay for men and women doing the same work
map.Paying every worker with a disability tw: Job-protected leave for workers with a new child

ww.Equal pay for men and women doing the sa: Equal pay between men and women comes from the Equal Pay Act. The ADA covers disability and requires reasonable accommodations for qualified workers.
ww.Job-protected leave for workers with a n: Leave for a new child falls under the Family and Medical Leave Act. The ADA deals with disability discrimination and reasonable accommodations.

map.Messages sent through email and text onl: Messages written in emails, memos and reports for coworkers
map.Messages sent in spoken words only, with: Messages sent through spoken words in meetings and calls
map.Messages sent only in writing on a page: Messages sent to customers rather than to coworkers

ww.Messages written in emails, memos and re: Emails, memos and reports are written communication, which uses words. Nonverbal communication relies on body language, tone and facial expression.
ww.Messages sent through spoken words in me: Spoken words are verbal communication. Nonverbal communication is what is conveyed without words, such as posture, tone and facial expression.
ww.Messages sent to customers rather than t: Nonverbal communication is defined by how a message is sent, not who receives it. It can be used with customers and coworkers alike.

map.Longer messages are always more polite: Readers pay more attention to longer messages
map.Short messages always hide the real mean: Messages can skip proofreading and editing

ww.Readers pay more attention to longer mes: Readers often skim long messages and miss key points. Concise writing keeps attention by cutting needless words so the main message comes through.
ww.Messages can skip proofreading and editi: Concise writing still needs careful editing. Cutting extra words and checking clarity takes effort, and it makes the message easier to read.

map.Selling to customers one time only: Tracking how many products a firm sells

ww.Finding new customers through advertisin: Finding new customers is customer acquisition. Retention is about keeping the customers a business already has so that they keep buying.
ww.Tracking how many products a firm sells: Tracking product sales is sales reporting. Retention focuses on keeping customers over time, which builds repeat business and loyalty.

map.Existing customers never need any servic: Existing customers cost less to ship products to
map.Retention requires no effort from the fi: Laws limit how much firms can spend on new customers
map.New customers always pay higher prices t: Existing customers receive free products from the firm

ww.Existing customers cost less to ship pro: Shipping costs are about the same for new and current customers. Keeping customers is cheaper mainly because attracting new ones takes marketing and discounts.
ww.Laws limit how much firms can spend on n: No law caps spending on attracting customers. New customers cost more because of marketing and promotions, which makes keeping current ones cheaper.
ww.Existing customers receive free products: Loyal customers pay for what they buy. Retention is cheaper because acquisition requires marketing spending, not because current customers get free goods.

map.Ignoring emotions to focus on rules and: Offering the customer a discount on the next visit
map.Agreeing with every demand a customer ma: Staying polite and professional during the conversation

ww.Offering the customer a discount on the: A discount is a reward, not empathy. Empathy means showing you understand and acknowledge how the customer feels about the situation.
ww.Staying polite and professional during t: Politeness is good manners, but empathy goes further. It means recognizing and acknowledging the customer's feelings, not just keeping a courteous tone.

map.Having a job that you enjoy every day of: Working fewer hours than a worker would like
map.Choosing not to work at all, for any rea: Being retired from work and living on a pension

ww.Working fewer hours than a worker would: Working fewer hours than desired is underemployment. An unemployed person has no job and is looking for work.
ww.Being retired from work and living on a: Retired people are outside the labor force. Unemployment counts people who have no job but are actively looking for one.

map.Acting on every feeling at once, whateve: Understanding what other people feel in a situation
map.Avoiding every stressful task at work al: Setting goals and working toward them with energy

ww.Understanding what other people feel in: Understanding what others feel is empathy. Self-regulation is about managing your own emotions and impulses in healthy ways.
ww.Setting goals and working toward them wi: Working toward goals with drive is motivation. Self-regulation means controlling your own emotions and impulses, especially when you are under pressure.

map.A product that has no features at all an: A sketch of a product kept inside the firm and not built
map.The final perfect version of a product,: A fully developed product launched after years of design work
map.A product sold only to investors and to: A product tested in a lab to meet government safety standards

ww.A sketch of a product kept inside the fi: A sketch is a design idea, not a working product. An MVP is built with basic features so that real users can try it and give feedback.
ww.A fully developed product launched after: A fully developed product is the finished version. An MVP is released early with core features so the team can learn quickly and cheaply.
ww.A product tested in a lab to meet govern: Lab safety testing is compliance work. An MVP is a simple working version put in front of real users to test whether the idea has demand.

map.Only a long list of competitors' names a: A list of competitors' names, prices and store locations
map.Only the founder's hobbies and interests: The founder's school grades and a list of past hobbies
map.Only the color of the logo and the name: The logo design, brand colors and a draft of the website

ww.A list of competitors' names, prices and: Competitor details cover just one small piece of the story. Investors also need the problem, the solution, the market size and the plan for earning money.
ww.The founder's school grades and a list o: School grades and hobbies say little about whether the business can earn a return. Investors look for the problem, solution, market and revenue plan.
ww.The logo design, brand colors and a draf: Logo and website drafts are branding details. A pitch must explain the problem, the solution, the market and how the business makes money.

map.Having every employee do exactly the sam: Having employees share the same job title and pay
map.Hiring only people of one single age gro: Having employees all work in the same department

ww.Having employees share the same job titl: Sharing a title and pay is about job structure. Diversity means differences among employees, such as background, age, culture and experience.
ww.Having employees all work in the same de: Working in one department describes where people sit in the company. Diversity refers to differences among the people themselves.

map.A promise never to quit a job at the fir: A contract requiring an employee to keep company information private
map.A guarantee of a yearly raise in pay for: A contract setting the hours and wages for part-time staff

ww.A contract requiring an employee to keep: Keeping company information private is a confidentiality or non-disclosure agreement. A non-compete limits working for competitors after leaving the firm.
ww.A contract setting the hours and wages f: Hours and wages belong in an employment contract. A non-compete deals with limits on future work for rival firms after the job ends.

map.Only the government of the state itself: The shipping company that delivered the blender
map.Only the injured user of the blender: The user, for choosing to buy it

ww.The shipping company that delivered the: A shipping company only carried the product and did not design it. The flaw is the maker's responsibility, and the seller may share liability.
ww.The user, for choosing to buy it: Buying a product does not make the user responsible for a flaw they could not see. The manufacturer, and possibly the seller, may be liable.

map.A message that only lists facts and asks: A message that reports news and updates to an audience
map.A message that forces compliance from al: A message that thanks readers for their time and effort

ww.A message that reports news and updates: Reporting news and updates is informative communication. A persuasive message goes further by trying to change what the audience thinks or does.
ww.A message that thanks readers for their: A thank-you note is goodwill communication. A persuasive message uses reasons and appeals to influence what the audience believes or does.

map.Only the competitors of the business, si: A plan that lists the goals of the business
map.Only the owner of the business, since no: A document listing the owners of a business
map.Only the managers of the business, since: A rule that managers follow when making choices

ww.A plan that lists the goals of the busin: A plan is a document. A stakeholder is a person or group affected by or interested in what the business does.
ww.A document listing the owners of a busin: A list of owners is a record. A stakeholder is anyone with an interest in the business, including employees, customers and the community.
ww.A rule that managers follow when making: A decision rule is a policy. A stakeholder is a person or group affected by the business, such as customers, suppliers or employees.

map.Learning only from books in a library or: Earning a college degree before starting a career
map.Learning only in school and then stoppin: Training for one specific job and staying in it

ww.Earning a college degree before starting: A degree is a single step early on. Lifelong learning means continuing to build new skills throughout a career as jobs and technology change.
ww.Training for one specific job and stayin: Training for a single job limits growth. Lifelong learning means continuing to pick up new skills so workers can adapt to change throughout a career.

map.Replacing all equipment every month of t: Buying insurance to cover the cost of machine damage
map.Repairing equipment only after it fails: Fixing machines after they have broken down

ww.Buying insurance to cover the cost of ma: Insurance pays for damage after it happens. Preventive maintenance is regular servicing done before breakdowns so the equipment keeps running.
ww.Fixing machines after they have broken d: Fixing machines after they break is reactive maintenance. Preventive maintenance services equipment on a schedule to stop breakdowns from happening.

map.Treating every customer the same, whatev: Setting a different price for each individual sale
map.Counting customers only, with no traits: Selling a product through several different stores
map.Ignoring customer data when planning any: Sending one advertisement to the whole population

ww.Setting a different price for each indiv: Setting a different price for each sale is price discrimination. Segmentation groups customers by shared traits so marketing can be tailored to each group.
ww.Selling a product through several differ: Selling through several stores is a distribution choice. Segmentation divides customers into groups by traits such as age or interests.
ww.Sending one advertisement to the whole p: One advertisement for the whole population is mass marketing. Segmentation creates separate messages for groups with shared traits.

map.A customer who avoids the store and neve: A customer who buys the cheapest product on sale
map.A customer who buys only once and then n: A customer who leaves reviews on many websites

ww.A customer who buys the cheapest product: Buying whatever is cheapest shows price focus, not loyalty. A loyal customer keeps choosing the same business over time.
ww.A customer who leaves reviews on many we: Writing reviews shows engagement but not loyalty. Loyalty is a tendency to keep buying from the same business.

map.Spoken agreements are always illegal in: Written contracts are cheaper to create than spoken ones
map.Written contracts guarantee that no one: Written contracts let either side change terms without asking

ww.Written contracts are cheaper to create: Writing a contract usually takes more time and money than a handshake deal. Businesses use it because a written record clarifies terms and reduces disputes.
ww.Written contracts let either side change: Changing terms without agreement is not allowed. Written contracts record fixed terms, and changes usually need both sides to consent.

map.To list every employee who worked on the: To explain the methods used to collect the report data
map.To replace the full report completely, f: To thank the people who helped write the report

ww.To explain the methods used to collect t: Methods are explained in the body of the report. An executive summary gives busy readers the key findings and conclusions in brief.
ww.To thank the people who helped write the: Thanks belong in an acknowledgments section. An executive summary gives the key points of the report so busy readers can decide what to read further.

map.Focusing only on closing as many sales a: Meeting the minimum standard the company sets for service
map.Following only the rules that benefit th: Smiling at customers while a manager watches the floor

ww.Meeting the minimum standard the company: Meeting a minimum standard is just following requirements. A service mindset means putting customers' needs first and looking for ways to help beyond the routine.
ww.Smiling at customers while a manager wat: Acting friendly for a manager is a show. A service mindset is a genuine habit of putting customers' needs at the center of your actions.

map.It will no longer need any customers at: It can set whatever price it likes
map.It must always produce less than other f: It can sell its product without advertising

ww.It can set whatever price it likes: Specializing does not free a firm from market forces. Customers and competitors still limit prices, and the main gain is greater efficiency and productivity.
ww.It can sell its product without advertis: Specializing does not remove the need to promote a product. The main benefit is that focus builds skill and lowers costs, making the firm more productive.

map.Copying a competitor exactly with no cha: Cutting costs by switching to cheaper materials
map.Keeping the same product forever and nev: Advertising an existing product more often

ww.Cutting costs by switching to cheaper ma: Switching to cheaper materials is cost cutting. Innovation means creating something new or better, such as a product, service or method.
ww.Advertising an existing product more oft: More advertising promotes what already exists. Innovation creates new or improved products, services or methods.

map.Money loses all of its value over a sing: Money kept as cash earns the same return as invested money
map.Money never changes in value over any le: Money gets more valuable as more of it is printed

ww.Money kept as cash earns the same return: Cash held at home earns nothing, while invested money can earn interest. This gap is why money today is worth more than the same amount later.
ww.Money gets more valuable as more of it i: Printing more money tends to lower its value through inflation. The time value of money is about earning potential, so a dollar today beats a dollar later.

map.Selling every investment at once for cas: Moving money into savings during a downturn
map.Putting all of your money in one single: Buying shares of the largest companies
map.Keeping all of your money at home in a d: Borrowing money to buy more shares of one stock

ww.Moving money into savings during a downt: Moving to savings is a response to market conditions. Diversification spreads money across different investments to reduce the risk of one loss.
ww.Buying shares of the largest companies: Buying only large companies still concentrates money in one type of asset. Diversification spreads money across different kinds of investments.
ww.Borrowing money to buy more shares of on: Borrowing to buy one stock raises risk. Diversification lowers risk by spreading money across different investments.

map.It measures a person's savings only, not: It shows how much money a person earns each year
map.It sets the price of groceries in all of: It lists the total value of the property a person owns

ww.It shows how much money a person earns e: A credit score does not record income. It reflects borrowing and repayment history, which lenders use to judge how likely someone is to repay debt.
ww.It lists the total value of the property: A credit score is not a record of property values. It summarizes credit history, and lenders use it to judge repayment risk.

map.Give rewards without any clear criteria: Give a bonus to the staff regardless of results
map.Criticize only mistakes and never praise: Point out mistakes in front of coworkers

ww.Give a bonus to the staff regardless of: A bonus that ignores results does not recognize good work. Recognition should reward specific achievements so people know what earns appreciation.
ww.Point out mistakes in front of coworkers: Pointing out mistakes in public embarrasses people and hurts morale. Recognition shows appreciation for good work through praise or rewards.

map.Shoppers who want only the cheapest opti: Young students who want low-priced earbuds for school
map.People who never listen to music of any: Families who want a toy for young children

ww.Young students who want low-priced earbu: Students seeking low prices are not likely to pay for premium sound. High-end headphones fit buyers who value quality and will pay more.
ww.Families who want a toy for young childr: A toy buyer has no need for premium headphones. The best target is audio fans who value sound quality and accept higher prices.

map.Only the weather on the day of the visit: The owner's age and favorite sports team
map.Only the name of the cashier at the fron: The brand of the store's cash register
map.Only the color of the store sign out fro: The year the store building was constructed

ww.The owner's age and favorite sports team: The owner's personal traits do not drive what customers buy. Buying behavior is shaped by customers' needs, income, culture and preferences.
ww.The brand of the store's cash register: The brand of a cash register has no bearing on why customers buy. Buying is influenced by needs, income, culture and preferences.
ww.The year the store building was construc: The age of a building does not shape purchase decisions. Customer needs, income, culture and personal preferences are the real influences.

map.It replaces the need for skills on the j: It lets you skip interviews when applying for jobs
map.It guarantees a promotion within a year: It raises your pay automatically after a year
map.It prevents you from changing jobs at al: It makes employers hire you without checking references

ww.It lets you skip interviews when applyin: Networking can lead to introductions, but employers still interview candidates. Contacts help you find openings and get advice, not skip the hiring process.
ww.It raises your pay automatically after a: Pay depends on performance, role and the employer, not on how many contacts you have. Networking creates chances and advice but not automatic raises.
ww.It makes employers hire you without chec: Employers still check references and qualifications. Networking helps you learn about opportunities and get advice, but it does not skip the hiring checks.

map.Taking every risk without thought, hopin: Buying products from the lowest-priced supplier
map.Hiding risks from owners and all of the: Forecasting sales and setting next year's prices

ww.Buying products from the lowest-priced s: Choosing a supplier by price is a purchasing decision. Risk management means identifying possible threats and reducing them.
ww.Forecasting sales and setting next year': Forecasting sales is planning work. Risk management identifies possible threats to the business and acts to reduce them.

map.A business that cannot ever earn any pro: A business owned by shareholders who trade stock publicly
map.A business with no owners and no legal f: A business owned and run by one person without a legal entity

ww.A business owned by shareholders who tra: A business with publicly traded stock is a public corporation. An LLC is owned by members and protects their personal assets.
ww.A business owned and run by one person w: That describes a sole proprietorship, where the owner is personally liable. An LLC is a legal form that separates owners' personal assets from business debts.

map.Loans have no costs at all for the borro: A lower rate means the loan must be repaid sooner
map.A higher rate always means better servic: A higher rate lowers the monthly payment amount

ww.A lower rate means the loan must be repa: The rate does not set the repayment time. The term does. A lower rate reduces the total interest paid, so comparing rates shows which loan costs less.
ww.A higher rate lowers the monthly payment: A higher rate raises the interest charged and usually increases payments. Comparing rates helps you find the loan with the lower cost.

map.Expenses are never paid by the firm at a: The business has too many customers paying in cash
map.Profit always equals the cash on hand: Sales are paid for in advance by customers

ww.The business has too many customers payi: Customers paying in cash bring money in right away, which helps cash flow. Cash shortages come from delays in collecting payments while bills come due.
ww.Sales are paid for in advance by custome: Advance payments bring cash in early, which helps cash flow. A shortage arises when customers pay slowly while the business has bills to pay.

map.A product sold only to employees at a de: A product that has been recalled and removed from sale
map.A product that is always given away for: A product that sells slowly and stays on the shelf

ww.A product that has been recalled and rem: A recalled product is withdrawn from sale. A loss leader is sold at a low price to attract customers who then buy other items.
ww.A product that sells slowly and stays on: A slow seller is simply unpopular. A loss leader is priced low on purpose to bring shoppers into the store.

map.Give a vague answer with no real details: Talk about your hobbies and life outside work
map.Say you have never had a problem at any: Answer in a few words and wait for the next question

ww.Talk about your hobbies and life outside: Hobbies do not answer the question. Interviewers want a specific example of a problem you solved, so describe the situation, your action and the result.
ww.Answer in a few words and wait for the n: A very short answer gives the interviewer little to judge. A strong reply tells a story with the situation, your action and the result.

map.Letting others handle everything while y: Completing your assigned tasks on time and leaving at closing
map.Waiting to be told every step of the wor: Following the same routine each day as directed by a manager

ww.Completing your assigned tasks on time a: Finishing assigned work is expected performance. Initiative means taking action beyond your assignments, such as noticing a problem and fixing it unprompted.
ww.Following the same routine each day as d: Following a set routine as directed is compliance. Initiative means acting on your own to start improvements or fix problems.

map.Interrupt them back every time they inte: Complain about the person to other coworkers after meetings
map.Stop attending meetings so you never hea: Send a message to the whole team about the behavior

ww.Complain about the person to other cowor: Complaining behind someone's back spreads gossip and does not help them improve. A private, kind conversation lets the person change without embarrassment.
ww.Send a message to the whole team about t: A message to the whole team publicly singles out the person. A private conversation respects them and gives them a chance to improve.

map.A required skill listed in every job adv: A formal complaint filed against a coworker
map.A fact proven by research about every pe: An opinion based on facts carefully gathered by research

ww.A formal complaint filed against a cowor: A formal complaint is a workplace procedure. A personal bias is an inner tendency to favor or judge based on preconceived ideas.
ww.An opinion based on facts carefully gath: An opinion built on gathered evidence is a reasoned conclusion. Bias comes from preconceived ideas rather than from evidence.

map.Mistakes mean failure forever for you: Success comes mainly from natural ability

ww.Feedback is useful for beginners: A growth mindset values feedback at every level of skill. Even experienced people use feedback to keep improving.
ww.Success comes mainly from natural abilit: Believing success comes from natural ability is a fixed mindset. A growth mindset holds that skills develop through effort and learning.

map.Punish only one of the coworkers and ign: Move one coworker to a different shift without explaining why
map.Ignore the difference completely and let: Tell both coworkers to follow the rules or face dismissal

ww.Move one coworker to a different shift w: Moving someone without explanation is unfair and creates distrust. A manager should discuss expectations with both coworkers and respect their differences.
ww.Tell both coworkers to follow the rules: Threatening dismissal skips the chance to understand each view. Clear discussion of expectations with respect for differences works better.

map.They guarantee a better hire every time: They help the firm confirm the applicant's right to work
map.They are required by law for every singl: They are the best way to measure job skills

ww.They help the firm confirm the applicant: Right to work is checked through proper documents, not by asking about family. These questions are not job related and can lead to illegal discrimination.
ww.They are the best way to measure job ski: Marital status and children say nothing about job skills. Interviews should use job-related questions to measure ability.

map.A contract is always spoken and a promis: A contract is for large amounts and a promise for small ones
map.There is no difference between the two i: A contract needs a lawyer and a promise does not

ww.A contract is for large amounts and a pr: No dollar amount separates a contract from a promise. What matters is whether the legal elements are present, such as offer, acceptance and consideration.
ww.A contract needs a lawyer and a promise: A contract does not require a lawyer. It is enforceable when it has the required elements, such as offer, acceptance and consideration.

map.Slides will not need a speaker at all: The slides will print poorly on a standard page
map.The audience will remember every word th: The speaker will run out of things to say

ww.The slides will print poorly on a standa: Print layout is not the likely problem with dense slides. The real issue is that the audience reads the text instead of listening to the speaker.
ww.The speaker will run out of things to sa: Dense slides usually give the speaker more to cover, not less. The main problem is that people read the text and stop listening.

map.A price set by government only, with no: The price at which a firm earns its highest profit
map.A time when demand is zero for every goo: The point where a market has a surplus of goods

ww.The price at which a firm earns its high: The most profitable price for a firm depends on its costs. Equilibrium is where quantity supplied equals quantity demanded across the whole market.
ww.The point where a market has a surplus o: A surplus means supply exceeds demand at that price. Equilibrium is where quantity supplied equals quantity demanded, so no surplus remains.

map.Selling at a higher price than all of th: The ability to charge buyers a higher price than rivals
map.Producing more of every good than others: The ability to produce a good with fewer total resources
map.Avoiding trade entirely with every other: The ability to sell a good in more countries than rivals

ww.The ability to charge buyers a higher pr: Charging more is a pricing strategy. Comparative advantage is about producing a good at a lower opportunity cost than others.
ww.The ability to produce a good with fewer: Using fewer resources describes absolute advantage. Comparative advantage compares opportunity costs, so a less efficient producer can still have it.
ww.The ability to sell a good in more count: Selling in more countries is market reach. Comparative advantage concerns lower opportunity cost of production, which is why specializing and trading creates gains.

map.Advertising only on billboards along the: Advertising to a large audience through television commercials
map.Selling only through stores and never th: Selling through wholesalers who resell to retail shops

ww.Advertising to a large audience through: Television commercials are mass advertising to a broad audience. Direct marketing reaches chosen customers through channels such as email, mail or phone.
ww.Selling through wholesalers who resell t: Selling through wholesalers is an indirect distribution channel. Direct marketing is a promotion method that contacts targeted customers directly.

map.A market with no buyers or sellers at al: A large market served by many big firms
map.A market owned by the government, where: A market that sells goods in other countries

ww.A large market served by many big firms: A large market with many big firms is a mass market. A niche market is a small segment with specific needs.
ww.A market that sells goods in other count: Selling abroad describes an export market. A niche market is defined by a narrow customer segment, not by geography.

map.Guaranteed profit every month, whatever: Receiving a steady paycheck from the start
map.No competition at all from any other fir: Receiving government payments to cover losses

ww.Receiving a steady paycheck from the sta: Entrepreneurs usually have uneven income at first. A steady paycheck is a benefit of employment, not a risk of starting a business.
ww.Receiving government payments to cover l: Government payments that cover losses are not a normal feature of starting a business. The real risk is losing the money that was invested.

ww.The firm's suppliers: Suppliers are creditors who are owed money, not the ones who owe it. In a sole proprietorship the owner is personally liable for business debts.
ww.The firm's employees: Employees work for pay and are not responsible for what the business owes. The owner of a sole proprietorship is personally liable for its debts.

map.Raise the price for that one customer on: Move the coffee to a harder-to-reach shelf
map.Ignore the customer and give no thanks a: Ask the customer to try a different brand

ww.Move the coffee to a harder-to-reach she: Making a favorite item harder to find does not show appreciation. A loyalty reward or thank-you recognizes the customer's repeat business.
ww.Ask the customer to try a different bran: Pushing a different brand does not recognize the customer's loyalty. A reward or thank-you shows the store values the repeat business.

map.Whether competitors have the same machin: Machine prices in a distant city
map.The machine's color only, not how it wor: Which option the owner finds more exciting

ww.Machine prices in a distant city: Prices in a distant city are a minor detail. She should compare output, long-term costs and demand for each option before deciding.
ww.Which option the owner finds more exciti: Personal excitement is not a business measure. The decision should rest on expected output, long-term costs and customer demand.

map.Hire only from one school near the compa: Hire relatives and friends of current employees first
map.Avoid posting jobs publicly and hire onl: Require a degree for jobs that do not need one

ww.Hire relatives and friends of current em: Hiring relatives and friends keeps the workforce similar to what it already is, which reduces diversity. Fair practices and wide recruiting improve it.
ww.Require a degree for jobs that do not ne: Unneeded degree rules screen out many qualified people. Recruiting from diverse communities with fair practices broadens the applicant pool.

map.Doing everything internally with all of: Building a larger staff to perform support tasks in-house
map.Reducing all quality to lower costs in e: Gaining direct control over suppliers' daily operations

ww.Building a larger staff to perform suppo: Building a larger staff to do support work is the opposite of outsourcing, which hands those tasks to outside specialists so the firm can focus on its core.
ww.Gaining direct control over suppliers' d: Outsourcing gives up some direct control because outside firms run the tasks. Its benefit is letting the firm focus on core activities.

map.An economy with no money and no trade of: An economy based mainly on trade with other nations
map.An economy run only by tradition, where: An economy where families make goods for their own use

ww.An economy based mainly on trade with ot: Trade with other nations describes an open economy. A mixed economy combines private business with government involvement.
ww.An economy where families make goods for: Families producing for themselves describes a subsistence economy. A mixed economy combines private business with government involvement.

map.Asking every customer by phone: A survey about customers' favorite colors
map.Counting receipts by hand only: A report on employee attendance last quarter

ww.A survey about customers' favorite color: A color survey would not show which product sold best. Sales data in a database report shows the best seller quickly and accurately.
ww.A report on employee attendance last qua: Attendance data says nothing about product sales. The manager needs a sales report that shows units sold by product.

map.It repeats forever with the same tasks: It repeats the same steps month after month
map.It has no specific goal at any time: It is completed by one person working alone
map.It needs no resources of any kind: It is managed by the finance department

ww.It repeats the same steps month after mo: Repeating the same steps month after month describes ongoing operations. A project is temporary, with a defined start and end.
ww.It is completed by one person working al: Many projects involve large teams, and team size does not separate projects from operations. A project is defined by its temporary nature and its end date.
ww.It is managed by the finance department: Projects can be managed by any department. What separates them from operations is a defined beginning and end.

map.The salaries and pay rates of all of the: Tasks, deadlines and the people assigned to them
map.Only the contact details of the project': The costs of each phase and the total budget

ww.Tasks, deadlines and the people assigned: Tasks, deadlines and assignments belong in the project schedule. A risk register lists possible problems, their likelihood and planned responses.
ww.The costs of each phase and the total bu: Costs and budgets belong in the project budget. A risk register tracks possible problems and how the team plans to respond.

map.Replacing the whole business every singl: Redesigning the whole process once in a few years
map.Changing only when customers complain lo: Checking final products for defects before shipping

ww.Redesigning the whole process once in a: A redesign once every few years is a big, occasional change. Continuous improvement means steady, small changes made on an ongoing basis.
ww.Checking final products for defects befo: Checking products before shipping is quality control. Continuous improvement is ongoing effort to make processes better over time.

map.A warehouse fire that destroys all of a: A theft of computers from the office during a weekend
map.A car accident involving a company van t: An employee injury caused by a fall in the warehouse

ww.A theft of computers from the office dur: A theft can only cause a loss with no chance of gain, so it is a pure risk. Speculative risk offers a chance of profit as well as loss.
ww.An employee injury caused by a fall in t: An injury at work can only cause a loss, so it is a pure risk. Speculative risk involves a chance of gain or loss, such as launching a new product.

map.Deleting old documents to free up storag: Storing financial records for tax reporting purposes
map.Keeping information secret from every em: Tracking the daily hours that staff work

ww.Storing financial records for tax report: Storing financial records is record keeping. Knowledge management captures, shares and uses what the organization knows.
ww.Tracking the daily hours that staff work: Tracking hours is timekeeping. Knowledge management captures, shares and uses what the organization knows so employees can decide better.

map.Let each employee keep personal copies o: Print documents and file the paper copies in cabinets
map.Never change documents once they are wri: Add new documents but leave the old ones untouched

ww.Print documents and file the paper copie: Paper copies in cabinets are hard to update and search. Reviewing and updating documents on a schedule is what keeps knowledge accurate.
ww.Add new documents but leave the old ones: Leaving old documents untouched lets out-of-date versions remain beside new ones. Regular review and updates keep company knowledge current.

map.So the files can never be changed again: So the files load faster when opened on a computer
map.So no one else can open the files at any: So the files are shared with the public online

ww.So the files load faster when opened on: Backups are copies kept for recovery and do not speed up the original files. Their purpose is restoring data if the original is lost or damaged.
ww.So the files are shared with the public: Backups are kept private for recovery. Sharing files publicly is a different action and could put business information at risk.

map.A method that focuses only on lowering p: A method for cutting staff to reduce costs quickly
map.A method where only inspectors are respo: A method of inspecting products at the end of production

ww.A method for cutting staff to reduce cos: Cutting staff is a cost-reduction step. TQM involves the whole company working to improve quality and customer satisfaction continuously.
ww.A method of inspecting products at the e: Inspecting at the end is quality control. TQM builds quality into every step, with the whole company involved in improvement.

map.Waiting for customers to complain before: Inspecting finished goods and discarding the defective ones
map.Making one large change and never changi: Redesigning the plant layout once in a few years

ww.Inspecting finished goods and discarding: Inspecting and discarding defects happens after the work is done. Continuous improvement makes ongoing changes to prevent defects and raise efficiency.
ww.Redesigning the plant layout once in a f: A redesign every few years is occasional. Continuous improvement means small, steady changes made on an ongoing basis.

map.Only the color of the email design and f: The software used to send marketing emails
map.Only the number of customers on the emai: The subject lines used in past campaigns
map.Nothing, because emails can be kept fore: How many emails customers opened last year

ww.The software used to send marketing emai: The sending software does not set how long data may be kept. Privacy laws and the company's retention policy decide retention periods.
ww.The subject lines used in past campaigns: Past subject lines have nothing to do with data retention. The company should check privacy laws and its retention policy.
ww.How many emails customers opened last ye: Open rates measure marketing results, not retention duties. Privacy laws and retention policy say how long personal data may be kept.

map.So that employees do not ask any questio: So that managers can punish workers more easily
map.So that only managers know the rules of: So that the company can avoid writing rules down

ww.So that managers can punish workers more: Policies are meant to set clear and fair expectations. Consistent communication and enforcement help employees understand rules and be treated fairly.
ww.So that the company can avoid writing ru: Rules need to be written and shared so that everyone can follow them. Consistent communication builds understanding and fair treatment.

map.Accept every request without question so: Add the change quietly and hope the team can absorb it
map.Ignore the client and keep working on th: Tell the client the change is free and add it to the plan

ww.Add the change quietly and hope the team: Adding changes quietly causes scope creep, which leads to missed deadlines and overspending. Each change should go through a formal change process.
ww.Tell the client the change is free and a: Calling a change free ignores its cost in time and resources. Each change should be evaluated and approved through a formal process.

map.Only the competitors of the company that: A document that sets out the project goals
map.Only the person who pays for the project: A tool used to schedule project tasks
map.Only the project manager and the people: A deadline set by the client for the project

ww.A document that sets out the project goa: A document of goals is a project charter or plan. A stakeholder is a person or group affected by or interested in the project.
ww.A tool used to schedule project tasks: A scheduling tool is software or a chart. A stakeholder is a person or group affected by or interested in the project.
ww.A deadline set by the client for the pro: A deadline is a constraint. A stakeholder is a person or group affected by or interested in the project.

map.So that taxes are never paid by the firm: So that firms can pay less tax than the law requires
map.So that every business reports the same: So that owners can choose the profit they report

ww.So that firms can pay less tax than the: Accounting rules do not let firms lower their legal tax duty. They make statements consistent so they can be compared and trusted.
ww.So that owners can choose the profit the: Consistent rules limit how profit is measured, so owners cannot pick the number. The aim is financial statements that can be compared and trusted.

map.Stop all advertising and sell only by wo: Open its own shop in the founder's home town
map.Sell only from the factory door to walk-: Add more candle scents to the current product range

ww.Open its own shop in the founder's home: One shop in a home town does not put candles in stores across many cities. Wholesalers or sales agents already reach retailers elsewhere.
ww.Add more candle scents to the current pr: New scents widen the product line but do not solve distribution. Wholesalers or sales agents are needed to reach shops in distant cities.

map.It sells only online to buyers who shop: It sells the candy directly from its own website
map.It sells through a few selected stores o: It sells the candy through a small group of chosen retailers
map.It sells only through one exclusive stor: It sells the candy through one agent in each region

ww.It sells the candy directly from its own: Selling from its own website is a direct channel with limited reach. Intensive distribution places the product in as many outlets as possible.
ww.It sells the candy through a small group: A small group of chosen retailers is selective distribution, which suits shopping goods. Candy is an impulse item and needs wide availability.
ww.It sells the candy through one agent in: One agent per region limits availability. Intensive distribution places candy in as many outlets as possible so it is easy to find.

map.Surveys can never support decisions in a: The questions were written in plain, simple language
map.Surveys are always too cheap to be trust: Customers' opinions do not matter for a launch decision
map.Customers should never be asked any ques: Surveys cannot measure what customers think about a product

ww.The questions were written in plain, sim: Plain questions help respondents understand the survey. The weakness here is that twelve responses are too few to represent all customers.
ww.Customers' opinions do not matter for a: Customer opinions are valuable for a launch decision. The weakness is the small sample, not the idea of asking customers.
ww.Surveys cannot measure what customers th: Surveys are a common way to measure opinions. The problem here is that twelve people cannot represent a whole nationwide market.

map.Always charging the lowest price in the: Setting a low introductory price to win market share quickly
map.Matching a competitor's price every week: Adding a fixed percentage markup to the cost of goods
map.Changing prices at random times for no r: Pricing a group of related products together at a discount

ww.Setting a low introductory price to win: A low starting price is penetration pricing. Price skimming starts high to earn strong profits from early adopters, then lowers the price later.
ww.Adding a fixed percentage markup to the: Adding a fixed markup to cost is cost-plus pricing. Price skimming begins with a high price and lowers it over time.
ww.Pricing a group of related products toge: Pricing items together at a discount is bundle pricing. Price skimming sets a high introductory price and lowers it gradually.

map.A route that is used only for products s: A route that moves goods from buyers back to the maker
map.A route that is used only for services a: A route that is run by the government for public goods

ww.A route that moves goods from buyers bac: Moving goods from buyers back to the maker is a reverse channel. An indirect channel uses middlemen between the maker and the final buyer.
ww.A route that is run by the government fo: Government-run distribution of public goods is not what defines an indirect channel. The term refers to using middlemen between maker and buyer.

map.A distributor guarantees every store wil: A distributor pays for the snack maker's advertising costs
map.A distributor always charges lower price: A distributor sets the quality standards for the product

ww.A distributor pays for the snack maker's: Distributors do not usually fund a maker's advertising. They help by reaching many stores and handling deliveries so the small maker can grow.
ww.A distributor sets the quality standards: Quality standards are set by the maker. A distributor helps by reaching many stores and handling deliveries.

map.A business that moves goods but never se: A business that carries goods between the plant and stores
map.A business that sells goods only to othe: A business that buys goods in bulk and resells to shops

ww.A business that carries goods between th: Carrying goods between plant and stores is the job of a transporter. A retailer sells goods directly to final consumers.
ww.A business that buys goods in bulk and r: Buying in bulk and reselling to shops describes a wholesaler. A retailer sells directly to final consumers.

map.Information that comes from the governme: Information taken from published industry reports and articles
map.Information that is purchased from a dat: Information stored in the firm's past sales records

ww.Information taken from published industr: Published reports were gathered by others, so they are secondary research. Primary research is collected by the business itself for its own purpose.
ww.Information stored in the firm's past sa: Past sales records were collected earlier for another purpose, so they are secondary data. Primary research is gathered fresh for the question at hand.

map.It guarantees that everyone chosen will: Researchers can pick people they think will give useful answers
map.It lets researchers choose only people w: It lets researchers survey the group that is easiest to reach

ww.Researchers can pick people they think w: Hand-picking people introduces bias. In a random sample every member has an equal chance of being chosen, which makes results more representative.
ww.It lets researchers survey the group tha: Surveying the easiest group is a convenience sample and can be biased. Random sampling gives everyone an equal chance.

map.Selling only to the largest customer in: Merging several small markets into one single market
map.Setting one price for every group of cus: Setting prices based on what competitors charge

ww.Merging several small markets into one s: Merging markets is the opposite of segmentation. Segmentation divides a broad market into groups of buyers with similar needs.
ww.Setting prices based on what competitors: Setting prices by competitors is competitive pricing. Segmentation divides a market into groups with similar needs.

map.Spend it on gifts for the owner's friend: Divide it equally among radio, TV, print and online ads
map.Spend none of it and wait for customers: Save it all for a big sale next year
map.Spend all of it on one large billboard i: Copy the ads that a large competitor runs nationwide

ww.Divide it equally among radio, TV, print: Splitting funds equally ignores where the target market is found. A small budget works best on channels that reach likely buyers.
ww.Save it all for a big sale next year: Waiting a year gives up sales now. A marketing budget should be used on channels that reach the target market.
ww.Copy the ads that a large competitor run: A large competitor's nationwide ads cost far more than $2,000 and may not reach her target market. She should choose channels that fit her own customers.

map.Setting one price for every product sold: Setting prices by what customers value most
map.Setting prices based only on the owner's: Setting prices low to win market share quickly

ww.Setting prices by what customers value m: Pricing by customer value is value-based pricing. Competitive pricing sets prices at, near or below what rivals charge.
ww.Setting prices low to win market share q: Low prices to win share are penetration pricing. Competitive pricing is based on what rivals charge.

map.They never require any employees at all: They are produced in advance and kept in stock
map.They are always made in big factories: They can be owned and resold by the buyer
map.They are always cheaper than most goods: They can be touched and inspected before purchase

ww.They are produced in advance and kept in: Services are produced and used at the same time, so they cannot be stockpiled. They are intangible and cannot be stored.
ww.They can be owned and resold by the buye: Buyers cannot own and resell a service, since it is a performance. Services are intangible and cannot be stored.
ww.They can be touched and inspected before: Services are intangible, so they cannot be touched or inspected beforehand. That is what separates them from goods.

map.Selling a product only to employees of t: Asking shoppers to rate a product already on sale nationwide
map.Selling a product at a loss forever in e: Launching a product in all regions at once with deep discounts

ww.Asking shoppers to rate a product alread: Rating a product already sold nationwide is a customer survey. Test marketing sells a new product in a limited area first to see how customers respond.
ww.Launching a product in all regions at on: Launching everywhere at once is a full rollout. Test marketing starts small in a limited area to learn from customer response.

map.Selling a brand only through one single: Changing a brand's logo to look more modern
map.Changing a brand's name every single yea: Selling the same product under a second brand name

ww.Changing a brand's logo to look more mod: A new logo is rebranding. A brand extension uses an existing brand name on a new product.
ww.Selling the same product under a second: Selling under a second name is multibranding. A brand extension uses an existing brand name on a new product.

map.Selling only through mail-order catalogs: Mailing printed coupons to customers' homes
map.Selling only at trade shows and local fa: Promoting a product through television commercials
map.Promoting a product only through printed: Promoting a product with in-store displays

ww.Mailing printed coupons to customers' ho: Mailing coupons is direct mail marketing. Social media marketing uses networks such as Instagram, TikTok or Facebook.
ww.Promoting a product through television c: Television commercials are broadcast advertising. Social media marketing promotes products through online social networks.
ww.Promoting a product with in-store displa: In-store displays are point-of-sale promotion. Social media marketing uses online networks to reach and engage customers.

map.Selling only the cheapest item in the st: Lowering the price of an item to close the sale
map.Selling only to customers who ask for it: Waiting for the customer to ask for help first

ww.Lowering the price of an item to close t: Lowering the price is discounting. Suggestion selling offers additional items that go with what the customer is buying.
ww.Waiting for the customer to ask for help: Waiting for a request is passive selling. Suggestion selling is proactive, offering related items before the customer asks.

map.Intensive distribution through every sto: Exclusive distribution through one grocery chain
map.A reverse channel for returned goods onl: A franchise arrangement with local grocers

ww.Exclusive distribution through one groce: Exclusive distribution gives one retailer the rights to sell a product. The farm is skipping stores and delivering itself.
ww.A franchise arrangement with local groce: A franchise is a licensing arrangement with other businesses. The farm sells straight to homes, which cuts out intermediaries.
